answers.answer: 4, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency

steps: The radius drawn to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.
That makes a right triangle with legs 3 (radius) and the tangent segment, and hypotenuse 5 (centre to external point).
By the Pythagorean theorem: tangent² = 5² − 3² = 16.
The tangent segment has length 4.
solutionReasoning.answer: 4, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency

commonErrors.remediation: Mark the right angle at the point of tangency first; it identifies which side is the hypotenuse.

steps: The sector is 30/360 of the whole circle.
The full circumference is 2π(5) = 10π, so the arc is (30/360)(10π) = 5/6π.
The full area is π(5)² = 25π, so the sector is (30/360)(25π) = 25/12π.

steps: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
This follows from the inscribed angle theorem: the two opposite angles intercept arcs that together make the whole circle, 360°, so their halves sum to 180°.
The opposite angle is 180 − 41 = 139°.

referenceExample.prompt: A cyclic quadrilateral has an angle of 85°. Opposite angle?
steps: Opposite angles are supplementary.

commonErrors.likelyCause: A property of parallelograms was applied to a cyclic quadrilateral.
commonErrors.remediation: Check the special case of a rectangle inscribed in a circle: opposite angles are 90° and 90°, which is both equal and supplementary — then test a non-rectangular case.

steps: The inscribed angle theorem states that an inscribed angle is half the central angle subtending the same arc.
The intercepted arc measures 164°, which is also the central angle.
So the inscribed angle is 164 ÷ 2 = 82°.

referenceExample.prompt: An inscribed angle intercepts a 100° arc. Find it.
steps: Inscribed angle is half the arc.

commonErrors.likelyCause: The inscribed angle was equated with the central angle.
commonErrors.remediation: Draw both angles on the same arc; the one with its vertex on the circle is visibly smaller.
